triage.note: TD-162 / D15. The door (TD-158) closed the PAID path and deliberately left the deterministic tier open — which left everything the free path costs unbounded: no rate limit, no request cap, no concurrency bound on the three `/api/extract/*` routes, only `MAX_BYTES` (25 MB) per document. A caller can post 25 MB filings in a loop (`jpm-2024`, the largest committed fixture, normalizes to 1,213,284 chars — the measured cost of one such request is in the red record), and `/api/extract/url` spends an outbound EDGAR fetch per request under this repo's declared fair-access User-Agent, so sustained abuse is attributable to the owner's contact address. The fix this case binds: a GLOBAL per-process token bucket (`src/sec10k/web/limiter.py`, stdlib only) consulted by one `@app.middleware("http")` choke point that runs before every `/api/extract/*` route — refusal is HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` and a reason in the standard `_err` envelope, BEFORE `extract_items` runs and before any EDGAR fetch. Global and not per-IP, deliberately: Zeabur's proxy makes forwarded-for identification untestable offline (the same reason TD-158's rate-limit branch was declined), and behind that proxy a per-IP key may be shared anyway. This case is deliberately not an AST shape read: the check IMPORTS `limiter.py` and runs the decision path with an injected clock (burst admits, burst+1 refuses with a positive retry-after and a usable reason, refill at the configured rate and never past the burst, `reset()` restores service, env config clamps garbage to defaults and extremes into [1, max] so no spelling of the variables means 'no limit'), then compiles the real middleware function out of `app.py`'s tree and CALLS it against a controlled limiter: under-limit reaches call_next; over-limit returns the 429 with Retry-After on all three extract paths (so a narrowed prefix reds however it is spelled) and never reaches call_next; `/api/meta` passes through without consuming a token; service recovers when the window elapses. An inverted test, an ignored verdict, a deleted middleware and broken env parsing all red functionally, not textually.
triage.note_negative_space: It does not prove fastapi binds the middleware into the ASGI stack (the standing app.py limitation, TD-38 — the live uvicorn over-limit run in tasks/reviews/pr-d15-red.txt is the end-to-end evidence), that the limit is fair between callers (it is one shared bucket per process, so one hammering client degrades everyone — accepted: the alternative is a per-IP key this repo cannot test, and the refusal names the shared limit honestly), that concurrency is bounded (requests admitted inside the burst still run concurrently), or that one admitted request is cheap — the 25 MB CPU/RSS figure is a measurement in the red record, not an assertion here. The paid path is out of scope entirely: the door (escalation-door) is untouched and still deliberately carries no rate limit of its own — the token is that path's brake, and since D15 the free tier's global limiter additionally sits in front of every extract request, token or not.
triage.sizing: Defaults SEC10K_FREE_BURST=20, SEC10K_FREE_PER_MINUTE=30: a human demo viewer runs a handful of extractions per minute (the deep link fires exactly one per page load), so 20-in-a-burst plus one every two seconds sustained is invisible to a person clicking; a loop posting 25 MB filings exhausts the burst in seconds and is refused with Retry-After. Bounds [1, 500] burst / [1, 3000] per-minute keep every configurable value a real limit.
